accountsLead: Connected mailboxes. Click for account settings, signature and servers.
accountOauthPasswordNotStored: The password for this mailbox is not stored.
applicationUpdatesDesc: New signed versions are checked automatically.
apiLead: Local access for agents and scripts. The server listens only on 127.0.0.1; every token is limited to the selected permissions.
apiTokenWarning: Copy the token now — it will not be shown again.
calendarHoursDesc: Time range shown in the week and day calendar views.
contactLocalOnlyNotice: This contact is stored on this device only: the account provider does not support contact sync.
tagsLead: Colored labels for messages. Create, rename, recolor and delete them. Tagged messages are gathered in the Tags section on the left.
exchangeConnectionDesc: Enter the domain account password. The EWS address was detected automatically; change it only if the server uses a different path. The password is stored only in Windows Credential Manager.
imapConnectionDesc: Check the incoming and outgoing mail servers. Use an app password for Mail.ru and iCloud.
jmapConnectionDesc: Enter an app password and check the JMAP Session address. The password is stored only in the system credential store.
mailPasswordDesc: The password is stored only in the system credential store. Use an app password for Mail.ru, iCloud and JMAP.
alignmentDesc: Left - next to the start of the message; right - at the right edge.
autostartDesc: truemail will start automatically and minimize to the tray. Open the window from the tray icon.
backupPasswordDesc: At least 12 characters. Recovery is impossible without this password.
calendarsLead: Calendars are now configured inside the relevant account: truemail detects CalDAV, Exchange or iCal automatically.
clearAllLocalDesc: Messages will be re-downloaded from the servers
codeExpired: The code expired or was already used. Select Connect to get a new code.
commandPlaceholder: Search: mail, contacts, commands, settings - any keyboard layout
confirmationCodeDesc: Copy the code from the Yandex ID page after signing in.
connected: Account connected: mail, calendar and contacts are ready.
connecting: Checking access and loading mail, calendar and contacts…
connectionDesc: The provider and available services are detected automatically.
connectSub: Enter any address — truemail will detect the provider and choose a sign-in method.
connectTimeoutMessage: Connecting took too long. Check your network and the server address, then try again
creatingStorage: Creating keys and the encrypted database…
dataFolderTip: Where truemail keeps the encrypted local copy of mail, attachments and the index. You can place it on a separate or encrypted drive.
diagnosticsDesc: Collects an archive of application logs where addresses, servers, folders, paths and internal identifiers are replaced with aliases. The archive is saved to disk - sending it is up to you.
enterCode: After signing in, paste the confirmation code here.
expertModeDesc: Show advanced settings and fields (most people do not need them). By default, only what is essential for daily work.
foldersLead: Map mailbox folders to truemail roles so unified "Sent", "Drafts" and so on work the same for every account.
foldersNote: Special folders are detected automatically, but you can reassign them manually.
globalShortcuts: Global (work even when the window is minimized)
globalShortcutsTip: System-wide shortcuts: they fire across the whole OS, even if truemail is minimized or you are in another app. For example, quickly compose a message or show the window without opening the app with the mouse.
importThemeDesc: A truemail-theme/v1 JSON file with theme, density, accent, and ui_scale.
keyBackupDesc: An encrypted backup lets you open the local archive after reinstalling or losing the system credential-store keys.
keySub: Move the mouse inside the area until the bar is full. The movements are used once and are never stored.
languageSub: You can change it later in Settings.
linkTextPlaceholder: How it appears in the message
localShortcutsTip: Work when the truemail window is open. Classic mail shortcuts for fast, mouse-free work.
minimizeToTrayDesc: The minimize button hides the window into the tray icon instead of the taskbar. Turn it off for ordinary minimizing.
notifyPositionDesc: Corner of the primary monitor where new mail cards and reminders appear.
oauthUnavailable: Account connection is available in the desktop app.
oldAttachmentsDesc: They stay on the server and download when opened
openingYandex: Opening Yandex ID in your browser…
previewLinesDesc: How many lines of message text to show under the subject in the list.
privacyLead: Secure settings are already active. Here is only what is genuinely up to you.
protectionDesc: HTML messages open without scripts in an isolated container. Remote images are blocked; you can allow them per sender. The database and local files are encrypted.
restoreArchive: Or restore the keys for an existing archive
ruleApplyExisting: Also apply to already loaded messages
rulesLead: Process new mail automatically: build a rule from condition groups and line up a chain of actions - a label, a flag, a move or a deletion.
securityLocal: All mail is stored locally on this device
securityRecovery: Save a password-protected key backup in Storage: it restores access to the local archive after reinstalling.
securitySub: Nothing to configure — secure defaults are already active.
securityTokens: OAuth tokens are kept in the system credential store
securityTracking: Tracking pixels and UTM parameters are blocked
sendToMenuDesc: Explorer context menu gets "Send to -> truemail": the selected files are attached to a new message right away.
setupWizardDesc: Choose the language again and connect an account.
showConversationsDesc: Group a thread into a single row with a counter (by subject and reply chain, within an account). Click to expand every message in the conversation.
smartLead: Folders that gather messages by conditions (all inboxes, with attachments, from today and any of your own). Reorder, show or hide, and edit conditions.
smartLogicHelp: Within each group choose "AND" or "OR". Groups are always combined with "OR".
storageLead: truemail keeps an encrypted local copy of your mail for speed and offline work. Here you can see what takes up space, where it is stored and how storage is configured.
storageSub: Encrypted mail, calendars, contacts and the search index will be stored here.
themesLead: Themes apply on the fly and change not only color but also element sizes. You can import other themes.
themeSub: You can change the theme, density and accent at any time.
toolbarLead: Choose which buttons appear above an open message and in what order. The toggle on the right shows the button; the arrows reorder it.
unifiedLead: Choose the physical mailbox folders that smart folders can gather messages from. By default all folders take part. For example, "All inboxes" additionally keeps only sources with the Inbox role.
unifiedNote: A folder disabled here will not appear in any smart folder. The conditions themselves - "inbox", "last 24 hours", "with attachments" - are edited in the "Smart folders" section.
welcomeSub: A fast, comfortable and beautiful email client. All your mail stays local on your device.
errorInvalidCredentials: Could not sign in. Check the account credentials.
errorNeedsReauth: Sign in to the account again.
errorRateLimited: The server temporarily limited requests. Try again later.
errorTimeout: The server did not respond in time.
errorCertificate: The server certificate could not be verified.
errorServerUnavailable: The mail server is temporarily unavailable.
errorForbidden: The server did not allow this action.
errorStorage: Local storage could not be accessed.
errorSecretStore: The system secret store could not be accessed.
errorCrypto: Local data could not be decrypted.
errorUnknown: The action could not be completed.
ruleFolderScopeNote: The automatic run reads working folders only, so the folder type offers Inbox, Archive and folders without a type.
ruleRunHint: Choose the folders: the rules will go over their messages, including those brought up by scrolling. How many messages one run handles is set in the "Limits" section.
sendersLead: Blocked and trusted senders and ignored conversations. The lists are shared by all connected mailboxes, and messages go to trash only and can be restored until it is emptied.
undoSendDesc: How many seconds a message waits before it is sent to the server. During that time it can be returned to the composer. Zero sends immediately. One value for all mailboxes.
outboxLead: Messages accepted by the app but not confirmed by the server yet: waiting for the undo window, scheduled, cancelled, and those whose outcome is unknown. This is a view of the sending queue, not a server folder.
absenceLead: A reply to incoming mail during an absence: once per correspondent, with separate texts for colleagues and external senders. The app picks the mode by the mailbox type.
absenceDomainsDesc: Senders from these domains and their subdomains get the text for insiders. Comma separated; the number of domains is set in the "Limits" section.
historyLead: Addresses you have written to from the selected mailbox. The recipient suggestion takes into account how often and how recently you wrote to them. An address removed here does not come back after a sync, but returns if you write to it again.
limitSectionMessagesDesc: How many messages the program keeps in sight and in memory
limitSectionRulesDesc: The size of rules, quick steps and one-off runs
limitSectionSendingDesc: The undo window and the memory of recipients
limitSectionOutOfOfficeDesc: When the auto reply stays silent and how long it may be
limitSectionMaintenanceDesc: Retention of service records and the size of background passes
limitPinnedPerAccount: How many messages can be pinned in one mailbox
limitPinnedPerAccountDesc: Anything above the limit cannot be pinned: the message stays in its usual place in the list
limitPinnedVisible: How many pinned messages to show at the top of the list
limitPinnedVisibleDesc: The rest are not lost, they are counted in the separator line
limitMessageFirstPage: How many messages to show when a folder opens
limitMessageFirstPageDesc: Fewer - the folder opens faster, more - fewer loads while scrolling
limitMessagePage: How many messages to load while scrolling
limitMessagePageDesc: The size of the portion added to the end of the list
limitSmartMessagePage: How many messages to load in a smart folder
limitSmartMessagePageDesc: A smart folder collects messages from several folders, so its portion is its own
limitMessageMemory: How many messages the list keeps in memory
limitMessageMemoryDesc: Messages above this number leave the list and are loaded again when you come back
limitSyncFailuresBeforeToast: How many failed mail checks in a row before an error message
limitSyncFailuresBeforeToastDesc: A short drop of the connection passes silently, a lasting one is reported
limitRuleGroups: How many condition groups one rule may have
limitRuleGroupsDesc: Groups are joined by "or": the message matches if any of them fires
limitGroupConditions: How many conditions one group may have
limitGroupConditionsDesc: Conditions inside a group are joined by "and": all of them must fire
limitRuleActions: How many actions a chain may have
limitRuleActionsDesc: One chain of actions for a rule and for a quick step
limitQuickSteps: How many quick steps can be created
limitQuickStepsDesc: Quick steps appear on the message toolbar and answer to hotkeys
limitQuickStepMessages: How many messages one quick step can process
limitQuickStepMessagesDesc: A selection above this number is not accepted by a quick step
limitManualRunMessages: How many messages a one-off rule run processes
limitManualRunMessagesDesc: The run started by "apply rules" stops when it reaches this number
limitManualRunBatch: How many messages a one-off run takes at a time
limitManualRunBatchDesc: The portion size: smaller - the program stays responsive, larger - the run is faster
limitUndoSendDefault: The undo send window on the first start
limitUndoSendDefaultDesc: How many seconds a message waits before sending while the setting is untouched
limitUndoSendMinDesc: The lower bound of the "Undo send window" field. Zero sends the message at once
limitUndoSendMaxDesc: The upper bound of the "Undo send window" field
limitRecipientEntries: How many recipients to remember per mailbox
limitRecipientEntriesDesc: Entries above this number are pushed out, the rarest first
limitRecipientTouches: How many uses to remember per recipient
limitRecipientTouchesDesc: Uses set the order of suggestions: more often and more recent goes higher
limitRecipientSuggestions: How many addresses to show in the recipient suggestion
limitRecipientSuggestionsDesc: The length of the drop-down list while an address is typed
limitOofSilenceDays: How long to stay silent after an auto reply to one sender
limitOofSilenceDaysDesc: Further messages from the same person within this term get no auto reply
limitOofMemoryDays: How long to keep the memory of sent auto replies
limitOofMemoryDaysDesc: The auto reply decides whom it already answered by this memory
limitOofMessageAgeHours: How old a message may be to still get an answer
limitOofMessageAgeHoursDesc: Older messages get no auto reply: after a long break the answer would go to all the mail that piled up
limitOofTextChars: How many characters the auto reply text may have
limitOofTextCharsDesc: The length of the text that goes to the sender
limitOofPeriodDays: How many days ahead an absence may be set
limitOofPeriodDaysDesc: The limit on the length of the "from" - "to" period
limitOofInternalDomains: How many own domains can be listed
limitOofInternalDomainsDesc: Domains whose messages count as internal
limitDoneTaskDays: How long to keep completed tasks
limitDoneTaskDaysDesc: A task marked as done is removed once the term runs out
limitIgnoredConversations: How many conversations can be ignored at once
limitIgnoredConversationsDesc: An ignored conversation moves its new messages to the trash by itself
limitConversationIds: How many identifying strings to keep per conversation
limitConversationIdsDesc: A message is recognized by them as a continuation of an already ignored conversation
limitIgnoreReturnWaitDays: How many days to look for a message in the trash when a conversation returns
limitIgnoreReturnWaitDaysDesc: Messages older than this term are not returned when ignoring stops
limitSweepMinDays: The smallest message age for automatic cleanup
limitSweepMinDaysDesc: The lower bound of the "older than N days" mode in cleanup by sender
limitSweepMaxDays: The largest message age for automatic cleanup
limitSweepMaxDaysDesc: The upper bound of the "older than N days" mode in cleanup by sender
limitPurgeBatch: How many service records to remove in one pass
limitPurgeBatchDesc: The portion size of background cleanup: smaller - it holds up writing to the database less often
limitRequestKeyDays: How long to keep the marks of sent messages
limitRequestKeyDaysDesc: By these marks the program never sends one message twice and keeps a cancelled message
limitRecipientOwnSendDays: How long to remember own sends for the recipient history
limitRecipientOwnSendDaysDesc: By this memory a sent message is not counted in the history twice
limitMessageTraitsDays: How long to keep the traits of vanished messages
limitMessageTraitsDaysDesc: By these traits a message is recognized if it came back to the server under a different number
limitsLead: The numbers that set how the program behaves. Every value has bounds; a value outside them is rejected with an explanation.
limitBackgroundSyncMinutes: How often to check the mail in the background
limitBackgroundSyncMinutesDesc: The ordinary check of the mailboxes. Messages on a live connection arrive at once and do not wait for it
limitOperationAttempts: How many times to repeat a message action after a failure
limitOperationAttemptsDesc: Moving, deleting and flag changes are repeated with a growing delay and then go to the failed list
limitGmailPollSeconds: How often to ask Gmail for new messages
limitGmailPollSecondsDesc: Gmail has no live connection, so the program looks into the mailbox itself. More often means faster mail, less often means fewer requests spent
limitSnoozeReleaseSeconds: How often to bring snoozed messages back
limitSnoozeReleaseSecondsDesc: A message snoozed until a time returns to the list on the next check
limitBackfillPage: How many messages to fetch from the server at a time
limitBackfillPageDesc: When a folder runs out of downloaded messages, scrolling takes this portion from the server. Smaller means the list continues sooner, larger means fewer trips to the server
limitBodyPrefetchMessages: How many messages to download in full after a mail check
limitBodyPrefetchMessagesDesc: A message downloaded beforehand opens instantly and without reaching the server
limitBodyPrefetchSizeMb: The largest message to download beforehand
limitBodyPrefetchSizeMbDesc: Larger messages pull their attachments in full and are downloaded only when opened
limitHistoryPage: How many entries to show in the recipient history
limitHistoryPageDesc: The page size of the history management section
limitRankFreshDays: Which contact with a recipient counts as fresh
limitRankFreshDaysDesc: Fresh contacts weigh the most, so the recipient comes higher in the suggestion
limitRankRecentDays: Which contact with a recipient counts as recent
limitRankRecentDaysDesc: Recent contacts weigh less than fresh ones but more than old ones
limitRankOldDays: Which contact with a recipient still counts
limitRankOldDaysDesc: Contacts older than this no longer affect the recipient's place in the suggestion
limitStageBatch: How many messages one processing pass goes through
limitStageBatchDesc: The portion size for sender lists, ignored conversations, sweeps and the out-of-office reply
limitStageSnapshotHours: How long a list of messages to clean waits for confirmation
limitStageSnapshotHoursDesc: An unconfirmed list goes stale and the confirmation has to be opened again
limitSweepWaitSeconds: How long a sweep waits for another action on a message
limitSweepWaitSecondsDesc: A message busy with another action is postponed and the pass returns to it later
limitSweepMaxWaits: How many times a sweep waits before giving up
limitSweepMaxWaitsDesc: After the last wait the pass is marked as failed and the messages stay where they are
limitSweepFullPassHours: How often to recheck every message from a sender
limitSweepFullPassHoursDesc: A full pass of an enabled sweep entry finds messages missed by the ordinary processing
limitReminderCheckSeconds: How often to check reminders about meetings and tasks
limitReminderCheckSecondsDesc: More often means the card arrives closer to the time, less often means the program wakes the computer less
limitUpdateCheckHours: How often to check whether a new version is out
limitUpdateCheckHoursDesc: The check runs in the background and installs nothing without consent
